title: MAC, ARP & Framing
html:
The last logical hop before data becomes a raw electrical signal.

DHCP — getting an address automatically

Definition

DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses to new devices joining a network, from a pool of available addresses managed by a DHCP server.

New device joins LAN
→
DHCP server (address pool)
→
Device receives an IP address

MAC Addresses

Definition

A MAC address (Media Access Control address) is a hardware identifier permanently assigned to a network interface — every network-capable device has one, distinct from its (changeable) IP address.

Within a LAN, devices at the Data Link layer communicate using these MAC addresses, not IP addresses.

ARP — Address Resolution Protocol

Definition

ARP bridges the gap between Layer 3 and Layer 2 — it resolves a known IP address into the corresponding MAC address needed to actually deliver a frame on the local network. Resolved mappings are cached locally in what's called the ARP cache, avoiding repeated lookups for the same address.

Frame anatomy

Before a network-layer packet can hit the physical wire, the Data Link Layer wraps it into a frame containing (at minimum):

  • The sender's Data Link layer address (MAC)
  • The IP address of the destination, carried inside the encapsulated packet
Network-layer packet
→ wrapped into →
Data Link frame
